references.text: Moses is instructed to appoint Joshua, son of Nun, as leader of Israel and to strengthen him for the task of leading the people into the promised land.
After Moses' death, the Lord speaks to Joshua and confirms that he is to lead the people into the land and distribute the inheritance to Israel.
The first time Joshua is mentioned as Moses' servant, the one who stood before him and served him.
Joshua and Caleb were the only spies who trusted in the Lord and encouraged the people to enter the land.
